input.quote: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no intellectual property, deliverables or data-licence provision. Cellco's custody obligations (Section 3.10) confirm the Receivable Files are held for the benefit of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee, and nothing purports to assign our IP or data to Cellco, so there is no walk-away issue. But the only IP-adjacent term, Section 7.5(b) (p0346), runs one way: it preserves the Servicer's processes, models and servicing software (acceptable as Vendor retention of its own tools and know-how) while leaving us with no licence at all in the Receivable Files, Monthly Investor Reports, records and other materials generated for us and stored on Cellco's receivables systems, and no limitation on the Servicer's use of our data. That fails the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business. We therefore add the shortest fallback clause alongside the existing transition provisions rather than upgrading to the preferred assignment construct, which would conflict with the Servicer's retained software rights.

proposal.summary: Add a fallback licence to Issuer deliverables and limit the Servicer's processing of Issuer data
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement lets the Servicer keep its processes, models and servicing software but gives us no rights in the files, reports and records produced for us, so we add the playbook fallback licence (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, with modification and sublicensing rights) and confirm the Servicer may process our data solely to provide the services.

ops.text: License of Deliverables; Use of Issuer Data. The Servicer grants the Issuer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense for its business the Receivable Files, the Monthly Investor Reports and the other reports, records and materials delivered or made available to the Issuer under this Agreement. The Servicer may process the Receivable Files and all other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Issuer solely to provide the servicing and custodial services under this Agreement.
